memory_update.text: ZIM, MATX, EXPD, CHRW, and CB form a compact US-listed watchlist for the maritime/geopolitical/weather logistics chokepoint node: two ocean carriers, two logistics/forwarding platforms, and one marine war-risk insurance candidate.

The node is not simply a container-rate story; insurance availability, route reliability, customs complexity, air/ocean substitution, and inventory-buffer services may become second-order bottlenecks.
Port operators, marine data platforms, privately held forwarders, non-US-listed global liners, and OTC/foreign-listed terminal owners remain under-covered in this US-listed pass.

Before escalating any candidate, collect live Drewry/SCFI/FBX rate data, Panama Canal slot data, AIS route data, Suez/Bab el-Mandeb transit data, war-risk premium data, and company-specific margin sensitivity.

Add ZIM as a direct, high-beta US-listed container liner candidate for maritime chokepoint-driven freight-rate volatility; keep evidence requirement high because container overcapacity can offset disruption benefits.
Add GSL as a containership capacity supplier candidate; the thesis depends on effective fleet scarcity, charter-rate benchmarks, and charter expiry timing rather than spot freight rates alone.
Add MATX as a regionalized and expedited Pacific ocean/logistics candidate rather than a pure global chokepoint exposure.
Add EXPD as an asset-light logistics complexity beneficiary candidate; monitor whether disruption increases solution demand enough to offset ocean-volume and pricing pressure.

Marine war-risk insurance should be treated as a regulated/financial input bottleneck in the maritime chokepoint stack; AON is a candidate for the broker/risk-transfer layer, but materiality must be verified.

Need a separate pass for non-US-listed but globally important leaders such as Maersk, Hapag-Lloyd, CMA CGM, DP World, PSA, COSCO, and major port operators; they are central to the node but outside this US-listed pass.
ZIM should be tracked as the direct US-listed container-carrier benchmark for route-disruption pricing power, but overcapacity and bunker/insurance costs are the key falsifiers.
EXPD is a second-order asset-light logistics candidate: the thesis is complexity-driven demand for forwarding/customs orchestration rather than pure freight-rate upside.
DSGX is an underappreciated software/data candidate for the node: ocean visibility, customs status, predictive ETAs, and trade intelligence may become more valuable under diffuse congestion.
IRDM belongs in the adjacent chokepoint bucket because GNSS jamming/spoofing and insurance rebates may create demand for resilient maritime communications/PNT services.
CB is a gatekeeper candidate because war-risk insurance availability can determine whether vessels transit high-risk corridors; materiality to consolidated earnings remains the main caveat.

Next Layer 1B pass should separately screen US-listed rail/intermodal, port-adjacent industrial real estate, inventory-heavy distributors, and regional manufacturing suppliers that benefit when maritime reliability deteriorates.

node: Maritime, geopolitical, and weather-driven logistics chokepoints
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded direct and second-order US-listed universe for a timing-sensitive logistics chokepoint node. The most relevant public-market exposures are container carriers with rate/route leverage, regional ocean carriers with shorter or differentiated lanes, freight forwarders/customs platforms that monetize routing complexity, and marine-risk insurers/brokers tied to war-risk coverage. Live freight-rate, port-congestion, war-risk premium, and route-normalization data are required before company-level conviction. Expanded a focused US-listed universe for the maritime chokepoint node. The strongest direct exposures are container carriers and containership capacity owners, while second-order exposures include regional ocean/logistics operators, asset-light freight forwarders, and marine insurance/risk-transfer brokers. This is a timing-sensitive node: company-level conclusions require live freight rates, vessel routing, insurance premium data, port congestion, and confirmation of each company’s trade-lane exposure. Expanded the US-listed universe around maritime/geopolitical/weather logistics chokepoints toward direct carriers, asset-light freight orchestration, insurance gatekeepers, maritime visibility software, and resilient satellite/PNT infrastructure. This is a timing-sensitive node: company inclusion is for research prioritization only and needs live freight-rate, route, port-congestion, insurance-premium, and customer-volume validation before any company-level conclusion.
